definition: Participants interpretation of their graphs to specific behavior.
additional_note: I changed this code to reflect how participants think whether it is easy or not to use the app in practice ways, as for the evaluation part, we will just use the experience valce-analytic tag.

definition: How participants used graph feedback to guide/change behavior.
Participant makes personal decisions about app or device settings—such as time window displays or alerts—that reflect intentional use and self-guided adaptation.
Whether participants are willing to recommend it to others or not.
Any suggestions the participant gives for improving the device, app, or videos.
The reason participant gives for recommending or not recommending.
Mentions of device interference framed positively, as a reminder or beneficial prompt for awareness or behavior change.
Describes instances where the device disrupted the participant’s routine or caused discomfort.
When participants describe checking glucose after meals, often to observe how specific foods affected their readings.
When participants describe checking their glucose readings before eating, typically as part of a routine or preparation.
How participants are engaging with the sensor and sensor app in their day-to-day routines.
Apply when participants mention frequent or repeated check-ins throughout the day, typically as part of a routine.
When participants describe growing frequency of check-ins as their curiosity, motivation, or awareness increases over the participated period.
When participants mention only checking occasionally, sporadically, or without building it into a routine.
Participant expresses mixed or conditional feelings—both positive and negative—about a feature or experience.
Participant expresses dissatisfaction, frustration, or discomfort regarding any part of the experience.
Participant expresses positive emotional tone or satisfaction related to any aspect of the device, app, or video.
additional_note: (When the interviewee specifically mentions a positive emotions, not a extended context when us the coder think the interviewee is expressing a good emotions)

definition: Participant expresses that a feature was confusing, hard to use, or not accessible.
Participant indicates that a feature, setup, or interface was intuitive or comfortable.
Participant describes the device as disruptive to daily life, physically or socially.

Use this tag when a participant’s statement suggests an emotional reaction, reflection, or internal response—even if they don’t explicitly label it as an emotion. This tag is not used to classify tone (positive/negative)—that's the role of the Experience Valence codes—but to signal that something emotionally meaningful is happening in the participant's interpretation, tone, or phrasing.
additional_note: The purpose of this tag is to flag emotionally rich passages for further analysis, particularly those that may reveal: 1. What triggers emotional engagement (e.g., a shared story, an alert, a graph spike) 2. How participants internalize or personalize the experience 3. Unspoken tensions, motivations, or affective shifts Do not apply if the participant is only giving factual or descriptive feedback with no reflective tone or implied emotion

definition: Participant describes seeing others with similar conditions, feeling seen, or identifying with peers.
Participants' evaluations of health videos as either helpful or non-helpful in supporting their understanding or usage.
additional_note: I changed this code from one side (being helpful) to evaluations (neutral). Although the three sample interviews all state the video being helpful, but we need to consider the chance that someone doesn't think the same.

definition: Participant mentions becoming more aware of their health, related diet habits, or related behaviors through the device.
A personally developed realization or understanding that results in a change to the participant’s own day-to-day outine, or mindset.

subgroup: Insight Leading to Personal Lifestyle Change
definition: Changes in food intake or portion control as a result of device feedback.

subgroup: Insight Leading to Personal Lifestyle Change
definition: Changes in physical activity based on glucose readings.
additional_note: This includes any moment where participants reflect on how using the device helped them better understand their own health and adjust their lifestyle accordingly.

definition: A realization or takeaway that leads participants to influence or adjust the behaviors of people around them, such as family members, friends, or coworkers.
additional_note: These reflections go beyond personal change to describe how the participant’s experience with the device prompted broader lifestyle awareness or adjustments in their social circle.

definition: Participant references food, exercise, or lifestyle choices tied to cultural upbringing, routines, or personal history that influence behavior change.
Mentions of other frequently used apps revealing participant lifestyle or preferences.
